text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Air links between Estonia and Scandinavia may be severed this weekend as Estonian and Scandinavian aviation authorities failed to reach an agreement yesterday on sharing air routes.

- Some 1,000 students protested at the government building against the decision to end travel subsidies to students. The government decided on Tuesday to extend the subsidies until the end of the year.
- Parliament approved a wage rise for higher state officials.
- NATO General James Jemerson visited Estonia on November 14-15 and expressed support to Estonia's striving toward NATO.
- A Tallinn police commissioner was charged with the organising of a murder. The officer found two killers for a woman planning to murder her husband.

- Tallinn city council may hold a vote of no-confidence against newly-elected mayor Priit Vilba and city council chairman Mart Laar. The newspaper says that the Coalition, Centre and Russian factions have reached an reached an agreement to that effect.

- The recently approved law on the protection of personal data is clumsily worded and may restrict historians' access to various registers. The definition of protected personal data is far too vague and can easily be misinterpreted.

- Police are investigating the affair of the illegal data base, which contains information on traffic accidents, cellur phone owners and data from the population, business and vehicle registers. The data base has been offered for sale by the compiler, who is wanted by the police but still at large.
- Estonian cellur telephone firm EMT is to increase itas share capital from 16 million kroons to 64 million kroons.
- Trade union leader Julia Dmitriyeva of the Narva-based Kreenholm textile plant has threatened a five-day hunger strike in her demand to achieve an average 17.6 percent wage rise.
- The furniture firm Standard has received several orders from the United States. The company is represented in USA by the American Eagle Trading Company.
